## 1a5c1ca86025

**A-1A5C-1 — reproduced production teaching-schedule defect; target left unchanged.**

Pinned generator SHA-256:
`a2ec54281d4905b8f5d64493d347136dc955c82b711fb8c3d48685fbb6f69094`.
Pinned rule hash: `85ff67d41b51`.

The easy default schedule at seed `424242`, requested sample index `1`, with
three demonstrations and one query, materialized accepted indices `[1,2,3,4]`
with zero rejections. All three demos contain exactly two hollow frame
components; the query contains exactly one. Therefore the plausible rival
“perform the intended interior fill only when there are exactly two nonzero
frame components; otherwise return the input unchanged” fits all demonstrations
but predicts identity on the query.

The query is inside the production materializer/validator domain. The selected
Racket output fills the one-cell interior at zero-based `(7,3)` with color 1;
the rival leaves it 0. Exact input, selected output, rival output, accepted
indices, commands, hashes, and differing cells are retained in
`checks/audit/1a5c1ca86025/counterexample.json`; the source episode is
`checks/audit/1a5c1ca86025/episode.jsonl`.

This target declares neither a lesson-identifiability hook nor a rival contract.
A repair should vary component count within each lesson or reject windows whose
demos all share the same count while the query differs. I made no source change
to this audit target.
